Child agent-1 received the argparse contract, wrote argparse.mjs, found and fixed a trailing-whitespace integer parsing bug, verified parsing and streams, and returned a completed handoff.

Session index maps the serial session id to the workspace session directory used by the single main agent trajectory.
Serial main agent probed normal and error behavior, implemented argparse, scheduler modules, and entry file itself, fixed a local cleanup issue, verified outputs and exit codes, and completed.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized pure Node.js ESM, .mjs suffixes, local imports only, manual argv parsing, exact output and error parity, /output placement, and black-box probing through the executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: After probing, the parent split work into three owned child scopes: scheduler/job modules, argparse parser, and entry file, while the parent retained the shared interface contract and final end-to-end verification.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 wrote the Job and Scheduler modules, agent-1 wrote parseArgs and corrected an integer-whitespace regex bug, and agent-2 wrote the entry file against the agreed imports and counting semantics.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent received all three child handoffs, used the child-written files together in /output, and the final artifact contained test11.mjs plus lib/scheduler.mjs, lib/argparse.mjs, and lib/job.mjs.
parallel.verification: Children ran scoped checks, and the parent ran nine executable-to-node comparisons covering normal cases, zero, negative, equals form, extra args, invalid ints, missing args, help, underscores, stdout, stderr, and exit codes.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished parallel work was visible at closure; the official completed evaluation passed all 202 samples.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same ESM, .mjs, no-external-module, manual argparse, exact output, black-box probing, and /output requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single main agent owned probing, parser design, scheduler library design, entry implementation, integration, cleanup, and final verification without delegation.
serial.implementation: It wrote argparse.mjs, scheduler/job.mjs, scheduler/scheduler.mjs, and test11.mjs, then edited job.mjs to remove unused unit validation and simplify registration.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial final artifact contained test11.mjs, lib/argparse.mjs, lib/scheduler/scheduler.mjs, and lib/scheduler/job.mjs; the entry imported the serial scheduler path and integrated the modules locally.
serial.verification: It compared the implementation to the executable over normal, zero, negative, repeated, help, and error cases; after discovering a harness exit-code capture issue, it separately confirmed matching exit codes.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished serial work was visible at closure; the official completed evaluation passed all 202 samples.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the prompt obligations and added probed behavior for normal, zero, negative, help, missing, invalid, extra, equals, abbreviations, and integer formatting cases before delegation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt obligations and independently probed normal, zero, negative, repeated, help, missing, invalid, extra, and expected-one-argument cases before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both covered the required semantics sufficiently to pass; parallel converted the probes into child briefs, while serial kept the knowledge in the single main trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel assigned distinct implementation scopes to three subagents and kept parent ownership of the shared interface contract and final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no delegation; the main agent owned probing, all file writes, cleanup, testing, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's ownership was distributed but explicit; serial's ownership was centralized. Neither left implementation, integration, assembly, or pipeline ownership missing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied children with a shared interface contract naming exports, file paths, imports, parser behavior, reference outputs, and the no-cross-scope rule.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not need handoffs or cross-agent contracts; it maintained module interfaces internally while writing all files itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel attempt introduced a coordination boundary, but the boundary was explicit and compatible; serial avoided that boundary by using one owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built a flat lib layout with job.mjs, scheduler.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test11.mjs produced by separate child agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a nested scheduler layout with lib/scheduler/job.mjs, lib/scheduler/scheduler.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test11.mjs produced by the main agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The file layout and authorship differed, but both implementations reproduced the same observable schedule and argparse behavior accepted by the evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All three children completed and their summarized results returned in the AgentSwarm aggregate before the parent started the final comparison run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; local edits and test results remained in the main trajectory and were acted on directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel required a join point and used it successfully; serial had no join risk because all work stayed local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote distinct paths under the shared /output tree, and the parent validated the resulting integrated tree after all child writes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files itself, including a later edit to the scheduler job module, and then tested the integrated tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-workspace writes but no observed collision, overwrite, or contamination; serial had ordinary sequential edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children ran scoped checks and the parent ran integrated parity checks against the executable, then official evaluation passed all samples.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local comparisons, identified that one diff report was a harness exit-code capture issue, separately confirmed exit codes, and official evaluation passed all samples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both reached evaluator-aligned acceptance; parallel relied on parent post-join verification, while serial iterated inside one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 281.441 agent seconds and completed comfortably within the cell budget, with three subagents and no timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 194.083 agent seconds, no subagents, and no timeout, then completed successfully.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more agent time and tokens due to delegation but did not suffer deadline pressure or incomplete closure; serial was shorter and centralized.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The completed official status evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial passed 202 of 202 samples. The runs differ in process, not outcome. Parallel decomposed the work into three scoped child implementations and then validated the integrated files; serial implemented and corrected the whole solution in one main trajectory. No evidence shows a realized adverse parallel coordination consequence.
parallel_contributors: The parent converted executable probes into a shared child contract and delegated non-overlapping modules.
The parent consumed completed child handoffs and ran integrated executable parity checks before final response.
serial_contributors: The single main agent performed broader exploratory probing before writing the modules.
The serial agent corrected local implementation and harness issues before final closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a flat scheduler/job module layout, while serial used a nested lib/scheduler layout; both were valid under the task.
Serial briefly reported a verification diff caused by its shell harness exit-code capture and then corrected the check.

candidates.reason: Parallel explicitly assigned implementation work to child agents for scheduler/job, argparse, and entry modules, then received completed outputs.
The parent owned the shared interface contract and final integrated comparison, so component reconciliation was not unowned.
The entry file was assigned to agent-2 and the final artifact validation lists the expected entry and libraries.
The parent retained end-to-end pipeline ownership by probing, delegating, joining child results, and running integrated parity checks.
The parent's executable probing informed the child briefs and did not leave implementation unfinished or shorten closure in a harmful way.
Parallel did not complete all investigation as a separate blocking phase before implementation; it delegated after focused probes and completed normally.
No indispensable implementation or integration path was deprived of capacity; all delegated pieces completed and were verified.
The fan-out was limited to three children, the run did not time out, and budget use did not displace required work or verification.
Each child scope was bounded by module ownership and every child completed with a usable handoff; no overbroad child left indispensable work unfinished.
The child prompts contained the environment, file suffix, no-dependency, parser, interface, reference-output, and scope requirements needed for their assigned modules.
The parent supplied explicit exports, import paths, method names, constructor signatures, and no-circular-import constraints before the agents wrote their modules.
No known finding disappeared during transfer; probed behavior was included in child prompts and completed child results returned to the parent.
The AgentSwarm result was structured enough for the parent to proceed directly to integrated checks; no usable result was left materially unconsumed.
No child or parent action consumed a superseded workspace or requirement state; the parent verified the current final files after the handoffs.
The child handoffs did not present incompatible contracts or reports; the final integrated parity tests succeeded.
The parent did not declare completion solely from child file existence; it ran integrated executable parity checks before the final response.
No replacement or retry child was launched, and no repeated work episode occurred without inherited state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: All three subagents completed and returned summaries; there is no explicit cancellation, stop, or interruption of a needed active child.
The completed module set was already present, integrated, and verified before closure; no ready candidate failed to be packaged or placed in time.
The parent ran integrated parity checks after the AgentSwarm child writes returned, and no later merge occurred without verification.
The parent received all completed implementation handoffs and exercised the combined implementation in /output.
There was no separate verifier child with a trapped finding; verification was visible to the parent after the joined implementation.
No child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; all three returned completed results and the parent verified the final tree.
The completed AgentSwarm result was followed by parent integrated verification and final reporting consistent with the child outputs.
The parent did not wait to a timeout or near-deadline state without inspection; the run completed normally and verified after child completion.
Parallel agents wrote different files under an explicit contract without overlapping behavior ownership or competing designs needing reconciliation.
No two live parallel agents edited the same source or configuration file; each child had a distinct file scope.
No parallel actor replaced, deleted, or wholesale rewrote non-entry source actively owned or produced by another actor.
Only the entry-file child owned test11.mjs, and no other actor overwrote the submitted entry after or during that ownership.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated another actor's final-tree provenance.
Although children wrote to a shared /output tree, their ownership was isolated by path and no unstable state or provenance problem materialized.
No generated fixture, cache, temp path, auxiliary implementation, or tool output from one actor was consumed by another as a contaminated reference.

cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 32 Level-3 candidates were explicitly audited; no directly evidenced parallel coordination episode produced lost work, omitted stages, deadline pressure, uninspected results, write collisions, contamination, or unverifiable closure.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No label was retained because the successful parallel fan-out, child handoffs, shared workspace writes, and final verification had no realized adverse process consequence.
